title: Ending a custom without ending tenderness
meaning: Your shared promises can stay honest after a custom ends when regret is not turned into an obligation to continue.
text: A shared custom may stop fitting although it once genuinely offered warmth. In the physical position of Anahata, the Hierophant expresses care through recognised promises and familiar actions. Justice in energy encourages honestly considering both people’s present capacities and wishes. Death in emotions brings the experience of an earlier form ending. A sound decision need not feel immediately easy because something familiar is still passing. Tenderness supports that difference by allowing both the need for change and the personal meaning of what will no longer be repeated in exactly the same way.

Suppose weekly classes no longer interest both people equally. You openly agree to finish the shared membership and choose another time to meet. **An honest decision can leave room for sadness about the former custom.** You can remember the familiar route and pleasant conversations afterwards. Those memories do not oblige continuation. They reveal what is being left behind and what you want to preserve in new involvement without attaching closeness to one activity.

The difficulty is requiring a fair decision to receive immediate emotional approval. Sadness seems to mean the agreement was rejected, prompting repeated explanations. Honesty becomes an argument against a feeling. Warmth remains when a shared decision may be reasonable while saying goodbye takes its own time. New care can appear beside regret instead of only after regret has completely disappeared.
